title: Conditional native material branches; reduced execution remains open
changes: Native elastic opening/compression candidates retain cohesive shear and full support force maps. Inspect vibration basis shows their qualification beside the 3D scene. Five scoped Windows suites, compiled native API, HTTP gateway and source registration pass. Reduced motion, strong sheet impacts and complete realtime remain unfinished; this checkpoint is not yet verified on Render.

Inspect vibration basis beside the 3D scene now separates native material preparation from explicit opening/closing contact curvature, including compressed geometry and torque. Independent scalar-gap/potential tests pass; native stationary force and contact energy reconstruct across glass/oak/iron/ice. Material branch, refinement, nonlinear trajectory, endpoint-history and full reaction transfers still block reduced execution. No accepted physics law or convergence gate changed.

Native relative contact differentials and correlated local-point bounds retain common motion, exact-frequency cancellation, finite Cayley rotations and sub-ULP axial gaps. Inspect vibration basis beside the 3D scene shows measured narrower gap uncertainty. All 54 modes and native histories remain; the sheet still has 116 uncertain sites and reduced motion is not admitted. No physical response law or tolerance changed.

Optional CPU heat remains on the same moving matter through flight/contact, with shared clocks, exact save/reopen and atomic rollback. Temperature inspection uses real field observations. Water continues the same sealed accepted state with cumulative budgets. Run, replay, reset, inspection and save controls are beside the 3D scene on desktop and phones. Representation, CUDA contact and material-loading workbenches use the same adjacent action dock; thermal navigation closes only its owned session.

Separate native 3D references: hinged bar with exact-equilibrium sleep/wake and support removal, conservative depth-averaged water, conduction/ice latent heat and closed fuel/oxygen/products. CPU contact forces now mark actual surface sample locations on both participants. These do not complete strong sheet impacts or cross-system coupling.

Shared CPU/CUDA box closest-point geometry now preserves tiny exterior gaps in local coordinates instead of producing an invalid normal at a rounded boundary. The measured native regression passes, and four-material CPU/CUDA, parallel/reference and 10 m rigid controls retain their gates. The page lists usable checks and clearly marks full smash tests and remaining representation families unfinished.

Representation workbench at /representations compiles adaptive occupied cubes and tests conservative CPU rigid/detail mappings and gravity-only flight. No internal/contact solver is connected there. Coupled lab now shows Before/Contact/After milestones and frames the ground in Full drop; the default test is plainly labeled a rigid rebound control.

Versioned geometry/law definitions and stable matter/instance IDs retain exact native state with Save scene / Open scene. Unattached spheres use a local numerical translation origin without changing physical state or history. Four materials complete the 10 m primitive control at two timesteps/contact phases and match an independent compliance oracle; the connected glass sheet still stops at its work bound. The page starts with a useful 10 m drop and clearly separates that control from fracture.

Coupled lab shows calculation pace in plain slower/faster-than-realtime terms and the failed full-drop boundary. The withdrawn local-force experiment is archived; published physics remains unchanged. Five scoped client/gateway CTests pass; complete drop/realtime gate still fails.

Parallel coupled CUDA skips guaranteed-zero separated-pair ledger groups in original addition order and computes shared initial geometry once per trial batch. Contact sites shows actual sites from the last accepted substep. The final permitted Newton update can pass its original residual tolerance without an extra loop iteration. Full impact accuracy and realtime remain unqualified.

Coupled lab adds Target view, Follow ball and Full drop with actual-position markers, simulated time, gap and speed. Run 10 steps shows its duration; Run to ball contact advances accepted steps with Stop. Edited settings are applied before Run and support motion cannot masquerade as ball contact. The exact replay log has a larger bounded storage allowance. Physics laws and gates are unchanged.

Coupled GPU lab adds Linear solve: Resident cuSOLVER on pinned Windows x64. Reusable buffers and device error status support actual changed-input command replay. Eight tested glass/oak/iron/ice histories match CuPy reference exactly. CuPy reference remains default; the full nonlinear loop is still host controlled and realtime remains open.

Coupled GPU lab tries the full Newton step first, then batches smaller choices on CUDA. Select Step-size probes to compare the retained one-at-a-time reference. Four-material accepted poses, velocities, material history and work records match exactly. Measured low-energy wall time improves 12–26%; full material accuracy and realtime remain open.

Ball / ground timing control uses explicit material/mass-derived contact refinement. Compare Before, actual accepted peak-impact microstep and Live. The derivative scale resolves microsecond contact positions. Connected sheets at refined contact phases still stop at the bounded trial budget; Reference remains their default. No whole-world realtime or material fracture qualification.

Coupled lab adds ranked Newton starting guesses and an explicit single-start reference. The same total 24-iteration bound and physical gates remain. Strong glass/oak/iron/ice controls now finish at both tested timesteps; trajectory differences remain substantial. Run 0.1 s displays actual accepted states.

Coupled CUDA fault collection now runs in parallel with unchanged fault priority and physical sums. The lab shows rejected-trial counts and rollback; its log records actual failed Newton inputs/candidates/Jacobian. Strong glass/ice convergence remains unresolved.

Coupled 3D lab now defaults to Parallel CUDA and offers Serial reference. Ordered material/contact contributions and current-Jacobian reuse preserve all four tested physical histories exactly. Controlled runs improve to about 1.4–3.0 wall seconds per 0.042 physical seconds; still far from realtime.

New /coupled 3D page: nine connected finite cells, density-derived ball, fixed supports, actual CUDA material/contact/body solve, Before/Live and downloadable complete microstep records. Low-energy four-material controls pass; fracture/yield and realtime remain unqualified.

GPU material inspector now shows actual CUDA force directions and body force/torque pairs. General finite-frame reactions use the same CPU/CUDA energy gradient; normal controlled loading has zero torque. The diagram still has no dynamics clock.

GPU material laws at /materials runs persistent damage and six-mode plastic return from shared C++ source via CuPy. Apply a common opening, unload and inspect retained history. Controlled constitutive loading only, not dynamic GPU fracture or dents.

PhysX reuses resident CUDA pose/velocity buffers. Every substep is retained; all 15360 refined stack states match the independent column reference exactly. The slower column path remains available in the profiler.
GPU lab shows actual SDK stepping, GPU observation and host audit time. Every calculated substep remains recorded; constitutive port is separate from this rigid solver.
GPU solver now compares Newton XPBD and PhysX TGS in the same 3D world. Stack control uses zero bounce/friction and 1/1920 s; glass/oak/iron/ice complete in scoped controls.
PhysX records actual CUDA poses, mass/inertia and normal contact impulses each substep. Friction and full contact/numerical work are not yet in that account; no bonded GPU fracture or dents.
Open GPU contact yard: CUDA-calculated ball drops, two-body impacts and free fall. CPU material lab remains available; no GPU fracture or dents yet.
GPU frames use actual resident Newton/Warp states, with every substep recorded. The full 27-block stack stops at an energy refusal and retains its last accepted scene.
Optional Contact response → Coupled friction + bounce solves sliding and twist together while retaining native material restitution. Reference stays default.
Physics step selects the actual 1/960 or refined 1/1920 s experiment. Before/Live shows original and accepted native geometry.

The reproduced refined glass refusal is twisting friction adding energy in the direction of existing spin. Terminal rejected records now retain original-cell impulses and actual force/solver velocities.
Glass/oak/iron/ice complete at both timesteps in the initial trial. Full convergence, large energy deficits, connected calculation speed and thermal/fluid/power laws remain unfinished.
